title: AI Made Devs 19% Slower (METR 2025 Study)
summary: Zencoder explainer: METR and DORA data, three hidden time drains (debugging, integration, review) and fixes.

verdicts.note: Accurately reports METR's July 2025 RCT (16 devs, ~19% slower); the finding is specific to that setting and early-2025 tools.
METR RCT: 16 experienced developers, 246 tasks in their own mature repos; allowing early-2025 AI tools increased completion time by 19%.

assertions.quote: After using it, they said they felt about 20% faster

verdicts.note: METR found devs believed they were ~20% faster while measured slower; other studies also show self-reports outrunning measured gains.
Developers forecast a 24% speedup and afterward estimated 20%, but were actually slowed 19%. Experts also overestimated, predicting 38-39% faster.

assertions.quote: across those same teams throughput was down 1 and 1/2%. Delivery stability was about down 7%

verdicts.note: DORA 2024 estimated a 25% AI-adoption increase associated with ~1.5% lower throughput and ~7.2% lower stability; DORA 2025 found throughput improved but instability persisted.

assertions.quote: they had less secure output, but more confidence that it was secure

verdicts.note: Perry et al. (Stanford, 2022/CCS 2023) found AI-assisted participants wrote less secure code and were more likely to believe it secure.

assertions.quote: writing code is less than a third of a developer's day

verdicts.note: Studies of developer time show coding is a minority of work; DORA and Faros 2025 found individual coding gains often don't translate into delivery throughput.

assertions.quote: reviewers stop finding bugs after about 400 lines of code

verdicts.note: The SmartBear/Cisco review study found defect detection drops beyond ~200-400 LOC per session; AI makes large PRs cheap to produce.
The vibe-coding review names a verification gap between generation speed and developers' capacity to verify. It doesn't measure PR size.

assertions.quote: before you prompt AI to build a function, you need to spec it out

verdicts.note: Clear requirements, examples and references reliably improve agent output; the caveat is that bloated context can hurt, so curation matters.

assertions.quote: That's not AI work. That's context work that a human should probably be doing

verdicts.note: Benchmarks and field studies show strong performance on well-specified, common tasks and weaker results on context-heavy, novel logic.

assertions.quote: you can just put the prompt in there as part of the pull request

verdicts.note: Capturing intent helps reviewers, but raw prompt logs are noisy; a good PR description serves the same purpose. Plausible, untested.
